question: Does the Sales team enter Amount directly on the Opportunity, or is Amount rolling up from Opportunity Products / Line Items?
why: Validation rules don't fire on an Opportunity when an Opportunity Line Item write is what changed the total, so a rule guarding Amount never runs in a line-item-driven process (admin/validation-rules, Questions to Ask row 1).
answer_shape: Given [Products are / are not enabled on Opportunity], When a user edits [Amount directly / a Line Item quantity or price], Then the validation rule [fires on the Opportunity save / must instead be a record-triggered flow on OpportunityLineItem].

question: Does any Workflow Rule field update, Process Builder, or other automation write to Opportunity Amount after the record saves?
why: Validation rules are not re-run after a workflow field update re-saves the record, so an existing post-save writer would make the new rule silently not a database invariant (admin/validation-rules, Questions to Ask row 2).
answer_shape: Given the current org automation on Opportunity, When Amount changes after Closed Won, Then either no other automation writes Amount post-save, or the named automation is listed and migrated to a before-save flow / accepted as an exception.

question: Which users, profiles, or integrations must still be able to save a Closed Won Opportunity that would otherwise violate this rule (e.g. data loads, an ERP/CPQ sync, a manager issuing a credit memo, admins correcting an error) — and who is the accountable owner when the rule blocks a save that should have gone through?
why: Every rule with no bypass blocks every data load and API write that doesn't meet the condition (admin/validation-rules, row 3); a rule with no named exception owner hides the trigger, the condition and the exception path from whoever hits it later (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 7).
answer_shape: Given a save that would violate the rule, When it is attempted by [named profile / integration user / admin], Then it [is exempted via Custom Permission '<name>' carried by Permission Set '<name>' / is blocked, and <named role> is who the user contacts to fix it].

question: What should the validation error say, in 255 characters or fewer, naming both the problem and the fix?
why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that can't say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence (admin/validation-rules, row 5, and the skill's Error Message Standard: what went wrong / why / how to fix).
proposed_default: "Amount cannot be decreased once this Opportunity is Closed Won. Amount is locked after close to protect the recorded deal value. Contact your manager to reopen the Opportunity before changing Amount."
answer_shape: The final message text, not a placeholder — under 255 characters, stating the problem and the required next action.

question: Does Opportunity data today already violate this rule — are there Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount has already been edited downward, or a legitimate recurring reason Amount decreases after close (refunds, credit memos, contract true-ups)?
why: Validation rules fire on update as well as insert; an active rule on dirty data blocks every future edit of every violating record except the one that would fix it (admin/validation-rules, row 6).
answer_shape: Given the Opportunity data as it exists today, When the rule is deployed, Then it deploys [active, because no known violations or legitimate decrease pattern exists] or [inactive with owner '<name>' and a target date for cleanup / for building the legitimate-decrease exception].

question: Roughly how many Opportunities move to Closed Won per day, and what is the largest single batch write to Opportunity anyone runs (data load, mass reassignment, a nightly sync)?
why: A requirement's volume and its largest batch decide whether an unbypassed rule turns a routine load into a failed job the moment it touches one non-conforming record (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 3).
answer_shape: A steady-state count per day and a worst-case batch size, so the rollout risk of Q3's bypass decision can be sized.

question: Does Amount on a Closed Won Opportunity ever get written from outside Salesforce — an ERP, a CPQ tool, a billing system, or any inbound integration?
why: A requirement sourced from or touched by an external system is an integration requirement wearing a validation-rule costume, and needs a pattern decision (bypass, or a contract change on the sending system) before this ships as a simple validation rule (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 4).
answer_shape: Given the systems that can write Opportunity.Amount, When one of them is external, Then it is named, its integration user is covered by Q3's bypass decision, and — if the volume or coupling is more than one integration user needing a bypass — this build is re-scoped from 'ask' to 'feature'.

question: Is Amount visible on every Opportunity page layout and for every record type this rule applies to?
why: errorDisplayField silently changes to Top of Page when the field isn't visible on the layout in scope (admin/validation-rules, row 4).
proposed_default: Amount is on the standard Opportunity layout(s) in scope; attach the error to the Amount field.
answer_shape: Confirmation that Amount is on the layout(s) in scope, or the error message rewritten to read correctly at the top of the page.

question: Does the rule's formula need to reference a compound field (Address, a person's Name) or a dependent picklist anywhere?
why: Validation rules can't use compound fields as of API version 20.0 (admin/validation-rules, row 7).
proposed_default: No — the rule references only Amount (Currency) and StageName (Picklist), neither of which is a compound field.
answer_shape: Confirmation the formula touches only simple fields, or a rewrite against the component fields before anyone starts typing.

question: Is there a workaround the team uses today to catch an Amount decrease after Closed Won (a report someone checks, a manual review), or is this a gap with no current safeguard?
why: Stakeholders often describe the workaround they built around a missing control as if it were the requirement, and an As-Is step tagged keep/drop/replace stops the new rule from re-implementing a manual process nobody asked to keep (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 1).
proposed_default: No current safeguard; the requirement itself states Amount 'can't go down' today, implying no control currently prevents it.
answer_shape: Either 'no current workaround, this is net-new' or the workaround named and tagged drop (replaced by the rule) / keep (runs alongside it).

question: Does this change require any new record-access or field-level-security restriction, or does the existing Opportunity sharing/FLS model apply unchanged?
why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places, and a validation rule changes neither by itself — an unstated visibility change would be silently missed (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 2).
proposed_default: No new record-access or FLS change requested; the existing Opportunity sharing and field-level-security model applies unchanged.
answer_shape: Confirmation of no sharing/FLS change, or a sharing_impact value naming the layer (OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rule, team, manual/Apex, restriction).

question: Who exactly edits Opportunity Amount — an internal employee, or does a customer, partner, or contractor with portal access ever touch it?
why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 5).
proposed_default: Internal Sales Cloud users (employees) only, consistent with the requester (Sales Ops) and no portal/partner access implied by the requirement.
answer_shape: Confirmation of internal-only access, or a licence_implication value naming the external persona and an escalation to architect/license-optimization-strategy.

question: Does this requirement need a new report or dashboard number alongside the rule (e.g. a count of blocked saves), or is the rule a save-time control only?
why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules forbid, and an unstated reporting need gets silently dropped between discovery and build if it isn't asked now (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 6).
proposed_default: No new report requested; this is a save-time control only, not a reporting change.
answer_shape: Confirmation no report is needed, or a reporting row naming base object, join chain, and whether rows must appear with no related record.
